newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Single currency will divide EU for years - Rifkind.
newsitem.headline: Single currency will divide EU for years - Rifkind.

text.p: British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind said on Wednesday introduction of a single European currency would divide the European Union for years.

"For the two main achievements of the EU so far, the common agricultural policy and the single market, all 15 member states fully participated. In deciding on a single currency the EU has taken a decision, which if it is implemented will divide the European Union for the forseeable future," Rifkind told a meeting of Dutch parliamentarians, civil servants and student.

Rifkind made his remarks following a speech he had delivered to a Dutch/British parliamentary friendship group in which he said Britain wanted closer cooperation between European Union members, while maintaining the nation state and veto rights.
"Now we are embarking on a new adventure which we know in advance is going to exclude at least half the enlarged European Union and seems to me an extraordinarily dangerous thing to do," he said.

"We already know that probably half the existing member states will not be able to join in 1999 even if they wish. And what about the 10 applicant countries? None of them will be able to join, in many cases for many years to come."
The EU is working towards a single European currency in 1999, and has set strict monetary and economic conditions which countries must meet to qualify for the project.
